claim: Holds a degree conferred by the National University of Singapore, shown by an NUS-issued OpenCerts certificate whose batch is recorded in NUS's certificate store and not revoked.

nullifier.derived_from: HMAC(server key, scope ‖ certificate targetHash): one badge holder per certificate

privacy.summary: Your browser hides every field except the degree title and NUS's details before anything is sent.
guarantees: Your name, student ID, date of birth and grades never leave your browser; the server only gets their salted hashes, which can't be reversed or guessed.
The server stores only the badge and a keyed hash of the certificate, not the degree title.
limits: Not zero-knowledge yet: the server sees the certificate's hash and its batch's Merkle root, which are stable identifiers. Anyone you've shown the full certificate to could link the two.
The degree title is revealed to the server when proving (it's how the server knows a degree was conferred).
trust: The zeroknowledger server, to discard the degree title and not log certificate hashes.
An Ethereum RPC provider sees the certificate and batch hashes when the server checks issuance and revocation.

changelog: First release: selective disclosure, checked against NUS's certificate store on Ethereum.
